note: The stage registry, as DATA. One declared list read by the writers, the scanner and
the reader alike, so that the rule -- every registry stage gets exactly one row in every
run -- is checkable rather than aspirational. Like the gate manifest .claude/close-gate.json (see
.claude/close-gate.json.example), it is repo-scoped configuration, and its gate_check bindings name
identifiers inside THIS repo's scripts/close-gate.sh.
THE DENOMINATOR IS len(stages), FULL STOP. `mandated_when` is prose here and nothing in this
release evaluates it. A conditional stage that did not apply is not an
absent row; it is a row in one of the reader's five states. Writing the condition down without an
evaluator is deliberate: it is the documentation an evaluator would turn into code, and leaving it out
would lose the reason each stage is here.
gate_check BINDS TO AN IDENTIFIER, NEVER AN ORDINAL. close-gate.sh labels its checks `5(journal)`,
`7(test-evidence)` and so on, and those numbers move whenever a check is added or inserted, so
the bindings below name the shell variables the gate
actually branches on (RUN_JOURNAL, RUN_EVIDENCE, ...), which do not renumber. An invariant
asserts every one of them still exists in close-gate.sh: renumbering the gate is then free, and
RENAMING it is loud.
available_from IS WHEN THE EVIDENCE COULD FIRST EXIST IN THIS REPO, not when the idea did. A run
older than a stage's available_from renders `unknown (retro)` and never `missing` -- reporting a
stage as skipped when its mechanism did not yet exist would manufacture a systematic false
finding across the whole historical corpus.
available_from_basis SAYS HOW THE DATE WAS ARRIVED AT, because some of them are measured and
some are not, and a reader cannot tell from the date itself. `measured` = the date the mechanism
first became available, followed by how that date was established. `repo-start` = the
`repo_start` value below, used where the stage is a human act
with no mechanism to date. THE RESIDUAL, STATED: a `repo-start` row whose practice actually began
later will score early runs `missing` when `unknown (retro)` would be honest. That is a wrong
answer in the accusing direction, and it is the one this file cannot rule out. It is cheap to fix
per row -- change the date and the basis -- and expensive to fix for all of them at once, so it
is fixed when a run is scored wrongly rather than by guessing twenty dates today.
retro_evidence SAYS WHETHER A STAGE CAN BE RECOVERED FROM DISK AT ALL, and null is a
load-bearing value rather than an omission. The stages divide in two: some leave an artifact
with the phase in its name, and some -- intent_gate, the two cross-checks, smoke,
independent_review, close_gate_task/phase, test_evidence, invariants, product_diff -- leave
nothing a later reader can find. `.claude/.last-test-run` holds only the CURRENT tree.
A null here is what makes the
reader render `unknown (retro)` instead of `missing`: accusing a phase of skipping a stage whose
evidence could never have survived would manufacture a systematic false finding across the whole
corpus.
changelog and cross_family_review are null DESPITE being recoverable in principle, and the reason
is the same in both cases: recovering them means matching CONTENT rather than a filename -- a git
range that touched CHANGELOG.md, or the `2nd-agent status:` line inside a qa-log fragment. Content
matching is the substring class the scanner's regression fixture exists to punish (a phase id can
occur in a qa-log only as a cross-reference inside another phase's fragment). Left null,
and left recorded, rather than done badly.
roadmap_row IS TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION FOR EVERY RETRO RUN and is emitted anyway. The run population
IS docs/ROADMAP.md, so a retro run cannot fail to have a ROADMAP row -- the enumeration source and
the evidence source are one file. It carries no information retroactively and only means something
for a live run. Said here rather than left for a reader to mistake for a check that passed.
retro_reason SPLITS THE TWO KINDS OF null, because they call for opposite
actions yet would otherwise render identically. `not-recoverable` means the evidence could never have survived
-- intent_gate, smoke, the cross-checks, close_gate_*, test_evidence, invariants, product_diff --
and a reader can do nothing about it. `not-implemented` means recovery IS possible in principle
and this scanner declines to do it, because recovering `changelog` or `cross_family_review` means
matching CONTENT rather than a filename, which is the substring class the scanner's regression
fixture exists to punish. A reader who sees the second one can act: implement the lookup, or
check by hand.
